/-!
# Erdős Problem 166

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/166](https://www.erdosproblems.com/166)
- [Sp77] Spencer, J., Asymptotic lower bounds for Ramsey functions. Discrete Math. (1977), 69-76.
- [AKS80] Ajtai, M., Komlós, J. and Szemerédi, E., A note on Ramsey numbers. J. Combin. Theory
  Ser. A (1980), 354-360.
- [MaVe23] Mattheus, S. and Verstraëte, J., The asymptotics of $r(4,t)$. Ann. of Math. (2024),
  941-965.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos166

/--
Prove that
$$R(4,k) \gg \frac{k^3}{(\log k)^{O(1)}}.$$

This is true, and was proved by Mattheus and Verstraëte [MaVe23], who showed that
$R(4,k) \gg \frac{k^3}{(\log k)^4}$.
This problem is #5 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.

The linked formal proof (Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol, via the construction of Bradač used for
Problem 920) gives `k ^ 3 / (log k) ^ c = O(R(4, k))` for a natural `c > 0`, with the Ramsey
number defined through `CliqueFree`/`IndepSetFree`; this implies the statement below.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos166.lean#L83"]
theorem erdos_166 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ (c C : ℝ), 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧
      ∀ᶠ (k : ℕ) in atTop,
        (SimpleGraph.classicalRamsey 4 k : ℝ) ≥
          C * (k : ℝ) ^ 3 / (Real.log k) ^ c := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos166

findings.description: The module bibliography's [MaVe23] entry (lines 28–29) gives the page range 941–965. The published paper occupies pages 919–941. This is only a bibliographic error; the mathematical statement and attribution are correct.
findings.source_evidence: The publisher's page for Mattheus and Verstraëte, “The asymptotics of r(4,t),” states “Pages 919-941 from Volume 199 (2024), Issue 2”: https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2024/199-2/p08. Its citation metadata also gives firstpage=919 and lastpage=941.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “941-965” with “919-941”; optionally give the complete reference as Ann. of Math. 199 (2024), no. 2, 919–941, DOI 10.4007/annals.2024.199.2.8.

reformulations.difference: The original UCSD problem asks for an eventual strict bound R(4,k) > k³/(log k)^c for some c, with coefficient 1. Lean uses an eventual non-strict bound with an existential positive coefficient C and requires c > 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: From Lean's bound, replace c by c+1. Once k≥2 and log k>1/C, k³/(log k)^(c+1) < C k³/(log k)^c ≤ R(4,k). Conversely, from the source's strict bound with exponent d, choose C=1 and c=max(d,1); when log k≥1, increasing the exponent only decreases the lower-bound expression. This equivalence was proved for an arbitrary real-valued sequence in /workspace/review/asymptotics.lean, without using the theorem under review. Positive real exponents were also proved equivalent to positive natural exponents by rounding upward.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found. The affirmative answer and research-solved status agree with the source and Mattheus–Verstraëte's Theorem 1. Lean checks established that the Ramsey defining set is nonempty, that classicalRamsey equals the linked proof's Ramsey number, and that R(4,0)=0, R(4,1)=1 and R(4,2)=4. The logarithm defaults at 0 and 1 do not affect an eventual bound. All 32 modules of the linked proof compiled successfully. In /workspace/review/validated_statement.lean, I derived the exact statement under review from that proof without importing the reviewed theorem; #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The only finding is the minor bibliography correction.
